mainTopic: אונאה and רבית with הקדש, and why land, slaves, documents and הקדש are excluded from double payment and the watchman laws.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a statement: with הקדש, even an overcharge smaller than the usual measure of אונאה lets the sale be undone. A ברייתא saying 'no רבית and no אונאה for הקדש' seems to contradict this. The גמרא reads it as meaning that only the ordinary one-sixth rules of אונאה do not apply. It explains that the ברייתא's 'stringency of the הדיוט' refers only to רבית, and that הקדש has too many stringencies to name just one. The גמרא then asks what a case of רבית with הקדש would look like. רב הושעיא answers with a flour-supply deal where הקדש always gets the better price, and רב פפא answers with building stones that are still חולין. Next, ברייתות use the pattern of כלל ופרט וכלל to show that land, slaves and documents have no double payment and are outside the laws of the unpaid and paid watchman. הקדש is left out of these laws by the word 'רעהו'. Finally, the גמרא begins a contradiction to the rule about הקדש from a משנה about shekels sent to the Temple that were stolen or lost.

steps.title: With הקדש, even a small overcharge reverses the sale
steps.stepSummary: The last words of a statement from before: for הקדש, even an overcharge smaller than the usual measure of אונאה lets the sale be undone.
steps.simpleTranslation: ...that even if the overcharge is less than the measure of אונאה, the sale is reversed.
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining the end of a statement that started earlier. It says that with הקדש, even a tiny overcharge undoes the sale.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With ordinary people, an overcharge must reach a certain size (one-sixth) before it counts as אונאה. This view says הקדש is treated more strictly: any overcharge at all, even below that size, lets the sale be reversed. This is the position the rest of the section defends.

keyTerms.meaning: Overcharging or underpaying in a sale
Less than the amount that normally counts as אונאה (less than one-sixth)
Goes back; the sale is reversed
Property belonging to the Temple

phrases.english: that even if it is less than the measure of exploitation, he may go back on the sale.

steps.triggerLanguage: דַּאֲפִילּוּ פָּחוֹת מִכְּדֵי אוֹנָאָה חוֹזֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a statement begun before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For הקדש, even an overcharge smaller than the usual measure of אונאה reverses the sale.

steps.title: A ברייתא says there is no אונאה for הקדש
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא saying that רבית and אונאה apply to ordinary people but not to הקדש, which seems to contradict the view that הקדש gets even more protection.
steps.simpleTranslation: They objected: Interest and overcharging apply to an ordinary person, but interest and overcharging do not apply to הקדש!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the view from step 1 with a ברייתא that seems to say אונאה does not apply to הקדש at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 1 said הקדש is stricter: even a small overcharge reverses the sale. The ברייתא seems to say the opposite: הקדש has no protection from אונאה. If so, how can anyone say הקדש gets even more protection?

keyTerms.meaning: Interest on a loan
An ordinary person, as opposed to הקדש

phrases.english: They raised an objection: Interest and exploitation apply to a layman,
but interest and exploitation do not apply to consecrated property!

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the rule stated in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that with הקדש even a small overcharge reverses the sale.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא plainly says 'no אונאה for הקדש', which seems to mean הקדש gets less protection, not more.

steps.title: Read the ברייתא the same way as the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is no stronger a challenge than the משנה was. Just as the משנה was explained, the ברייתא means the usual rules and limits of אונאה do not apply to הקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is this any stronger than our משנה, which we explained as talking about the rules of אונאה? Here too: interest and the rules of אונאה apply to an ordinary person, but interest and the rules of אונאה do not apply to הקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by reading the ברייתא the same way it already read the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה also said 'no אונאה for הקדש', and it was already explained to mean the usual system of אונאה (with its one-sixth limit) does not apply. The ברייתא can be read the same way. 'No אונאה' means 'not the ordinary rules', not 'no protection at all'.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it any stronger? (this source is no harder than one we already answered)
We explained it as referring to a certain case
Under the system or rules of אונאה
The law and limits of אונאה

steps.confusionAlert: 'No אונאה for הקדש' does not mean you may overcharge הקדש. It means the normal limits do not apply, so הקדש is protected even from small overcharges.

phrases.english: Is it stronger than our mishna,
which we established as referring to the system of exploitation?

phrases.aramaic: הָכִי נָמֵי: רִבִּית וְדִין אוֹנָאָה לַהֶדְיוֹט,
phrases.english: So too here: interest and the law of exploitation apply to a layman,
but interest and the law of exploitation do not apply to consecrated property.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי אַלִּימָא מִמַּתְנִיתִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the source to match an earlier explanation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to say הקדש has no protection from overcharging.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא means the usual one-sixth rules do not apply to הקדש, so even a small overcharge counts.

steps.title: The end of the ברייתא calls the הדיוט stricter
steps.stepSummary: If הקדש is treated more strictly about אונאה, how can the end of the ברייתא say 'this is a stringency of the הדיוט over הקדש'?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, how does that fit with what the end of the ברייתא teaches: 'This is a stringency of the ordinary person over הקדש'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer of step 3 using the last line of the same ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא ends by saying the הדיוט is treated more strictly than הקדש. But step 3 just said that with אונאה, הקדש is the stricter one. So the ending seems to contradict that reading.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
The end part of a teaching
A stringency; a stricter rule

phrases.english: If so, is that what is taught in the latter clause:
This is the stringency with regard to a layman over consecrated property?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, הַיְינוּ דְּקָתָנֵי סֵיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading given in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that הקדש is stricter about אונאה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's ending calls the הדיוט the stricter one, which does not fit a reading where הקדש is stricter.

steps.title: That stringency is only about רבית
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that 'the stringency of the הדיוט' refers only to רבית, not to אונאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It refers to interest!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers step 4 in one word: the line about the הדיוט being stricter is about רבית only.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With רבית the הדיוט really is protected more, because the laws of רבית do not apply to הקדש. So the ending of the ברייתא is true for רבית and says nothing against הקדש being stricter about אונאה.

keyTerms.meaning: About interest; this refers to רבית

phrases.english: It refers to interest!
phrases.notes: Only the רבית half of the ברייתא makes the הדיוט stricter.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַרִבִּית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the clause
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ending seemed to cover both רבית and אונאה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ending refers only to רבית.

steps.title: Then list the הקדש stringency about אונאה too
steps.stepSummary: If the ברייתא points out the stringency of the הדיוט about רבית, it should also point out the stringency of הקדש about אונאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let it also teach: 'This is a stringency of הקדש over the ordinary person', about אונאה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes further. If the ברייתא lists one side's stringency, why not the other side's as well?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the reading of step 3, the ברייתא contains two opposite stringencies: רבית is stricter for the הדיוט, and אונאה is stricter for הקדש. It is strange to mention only the first. The silence about the second suggests the reading might be wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it also teach
About overcharging

phrases.english: Let it also teach:
This is the stringency with regard to consecrated property over a layman, regarding exploitation!

steps.triggerLanguage: לִיתְנֵי נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's wording under the reading of steps 3 and 5.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If both sides have a stringency, the ברייתא should mention both. Mentioning only one suggests הקדש is not stricter about אונאה.

steps.title: הקדש has too many stringencies to list just one
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the question. The הדיוט has only this one stringency over הקדש, so it can be named. הקדש has many stringencies, so you cannot name one as if it were the only one.
steps.simpleTranslation: How can you compare? It makes sense to say 'this is the stringency of the ordinary person over הקדש, and nothing more.' But for הקדש, could you say 'this is the stringency, and nothing more'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back the question of step 6. It explains why the ברייתא lists only the הדיוט's stringency.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'this is the stringency' suggests it is the only one. That fits the הדיוט, who has just this one stringency over הקדש. הקדש has many stringencies over ordinary property, so naming just one would be misleading. The reading of the ברייתא therefore stands.

keyTerms.meaning: How can you compare? (rejects the comparison)
It makes sense that...
And nothing more

steps.whatToRemember: Saying 'no אונאה for הקדש' means the usual one-sixth rules do not apply, so הקדש is protected even from small overcharges. The ברייתא's 'stringency of the הדיוט' refers only to רבית. It does not mention הקדש's stringency because הקדש has many.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that 'this is the stringency' in a ברייתא can mean 'this is the only one', which explains why only the side with a single stringency gets listed.

phrases.english: How can these be compared?
It is fine to say: This is the stringency with regard to a layman over consecrated property,
and nothing more.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא הֶקְדֵּשׁ, זֶה חוֹמֶר וְתוּ לָא?
phrases.english: But with consecrated property, can you say: This is the stringency, and nothing more?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי הַשְׁתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the question of step 6.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The demand that the ברייתא list the stringency of הקדש.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The phrase 'this is the stringency' means 'the only one'. That fits the הדיוט but cannot fit הקדש, which has many stringencies.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The reading stands: הקדש is stricter about אונאה, and the ברייתא's ending refers only to רבית.

steps.title: What case of רבית with consecrated property is meant?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case of רבית with הקדש the ברייתא means. The obvious case, a גזבר lending הקדש money at interest, does not work, because the money would become חולין.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case of רבית with הקדש? If you say the treasurer lent a hundred to be paid back as a hundred and twenty, then the treasurer committed מעילה. Once he did that, the money became חולין and belongs to a הדיוט, so the normal רבית rules would apply.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what real case the ברייתא has in mind when it says רבית does not apply to הקדש. It tests the simplest case and shows it cannot work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the גזבר lends out הקדש money, he misuses holy property, which is מעילה. מעילה takes the money out of its holy status, so it becomes ordinary money and the normal רבית rules apply. So the case cannot be a simple loan of הקדש money, and the גמרא needs a different case.

keyTerms.meaning: Interest; extra payment for a loan, which the Torah forbids
The treasurer of the בית המקדש funds
Committed מעילה, meaning misuse of holy property
Ordinary, non-holy property
An ordinary person, as opposed to הקדש

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not whether רבית with הקדש is allowed. The ברייתא already said the רבית rules do not apply there. The question is only what real case that could describe.

phrases.english: Ribbis of consecrated property, what is the case?
If you say that the treasurer lent
one hundred for one hundred and twenty,
phrases.notes: He means the borrower gets a hundred now and pays back a hundred and twenty later.

phrases.english: but didn't the treasurer commit misuse of holy property?
And once the treasurer misused it,
his money went out to non-holy status,
and it is now the money of an ordinary person!

steps.triggerLanguage: רִבִּית דְּהֶקְדֵּשׁ הֵיכִי דָמֵי? אִילֵּימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After establishing that the הדיוט's only stringency is רבית, the גמרא asks what a רבית case involving הקדש would look like.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A real case where רבית involves הקדש without the money becoming חולין through מעילה.

steps.title: רב הושעיא: a flour-supply deal with the Temple
steps.stepSummary: רב הושעיא says the case is someone who agreed to supply flour to the בית המקדש at four סאה per סלע, and then the market price rose to three סאה per סלע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הושעיא said: What case are we dealing with? Someone took on the job of supplying fine flour at four סאה per סלע, and the price went up to three סאה per סלע.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הושעיא gives a case of רבית with הקדש that does not involve lending out holy money. It is a supply deal for flour.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The supplier agreed to a fixed price ahead of time. The market then went up, so the supplier now gives more flour than the money is worth. Between two ordinary people, a deal like this can count as רבית, but with הקדש it is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? A formula used to narrow down a case
To supply
Fine flour, used for מנחות

phrases.english: Rav Hoshaya said:
With what are we dealing here?
For example, where he took upon himself
to supply fine flour at four,
phrases.notes: "At four" means four סאה of flour for each סלע coin.

phrases.english: and the price stood at three.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוֹשַׁעְיָא: הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 8 by giving a case that does not involve lending out הקדש money.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The case is a flour-supply deal at a fixed price where the market price rose, so הקדש receives more than market value.

steps.title: A ברייתא: the Temple always gets the better deal
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא supports רב הושעיא. Whether the price goes up or down, the supplier gives flour at the rate that is better for הקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: If someone agreed to supply flour at four, and the price became three, he still supplies at four. If he agreed at three and the price became four, he supplies at four. This is because the hand of הקדש is on top.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to show that this flour case is a real הלכה, and that in it הקדש always wins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the price rises, the supplier must keep his deal and give four סאה. If the price falls, הקדש gets the new, cheaper rate of four. The rule is that הקדש always gets the better side, and this kind of deal is the רבית that is allowed with הקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is taught in a ברייתא
The hand of הקדש is on top, meaning הקדש always gets the better deal

steps.whyThisMatters: The ברייתא shows the principle behind רב הושעיא's case: הקדש is never the loser in a deal, even where a הדיוט could not make such terms.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא:
One who takes upon himself to supply fine flour at four
and the price stood at three, he supplies at four;
if he agreed at three and the price stood at four,
he supplies at four,
because the hand of the Temple is on top.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּדְתַנְיָא: הַמְקַבֵּל עָלָיו לְסַפֵּק סְלָתוֹת מֵאַרְבַּע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא supporting the case רב הושעיא described.
steps.raayaObject: רב הושעיא's case of flour supply as the רבית permitted with הקדש
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא ruling that the supplier gives at the rate that benefits הקדש, because יד הקדש על העליונה

steps.title: רב פפא: building stones not yet consecrated
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא gives a different case: building stones given to the גזבר that are still חולין, following שמואל's rule that one builds with חולין and consecrates afterward.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Here we are dealing with building stones handed over to the treasurer. This follows שמואל, who said: One builds with חולין materials, and afterward one consecrates them.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא offers another answer to the question of Step 8. The רבית case is a loan of building materials that belong to the Temple's project but are still חולין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the stones are still חולין, lending them is not מעילה, so the problem of Step 8 does not arise. Still, they are set aside for the בית המקדש and held by the גזבר, so the רבית rules do not apply to them.

keyTerms.meaning: Building stones
That are handed over to the treasurer
One builds with non-holy materials and consecrates them afterward

steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers for רבית with הקדש. רב הושעיא says it is a flour-supply deal where הקדש gets the better price. רב פפא says it is a loan of building stones that are still חולין but belong to the Temple's project.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Here, with building stones
that are handed over to the treasurer, we are dealing,
in line with שמואל, as שמואל said:
One builds with non-holy materials,
and afterward one consecrates them.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: הָכָא בְּאַבְנֵי בִנְיָן הַמְּסוּרוֹת לְגִזְבָּר עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, different answer to the question of Step 8, alongside רב הושעיא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The case is building stones held by the גזבר that are still חולין under שמואל's rule, so lending them is not מעילה, but רבית rules still do not apply.

steps.title: Where do we learn there is no double payment for these items?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה: עבדים, שטרות, קרקעות, and הקדש have no תשלומי כפל. It asks for the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: they have no double payment, and so on. Where do we learn this from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting the next part of the משנה and asking for its source. This sets up the derivation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A thief usually pays כפל, double the value. The משנה said this does not apply to slaves, documents, land, and הקדש. The גמרא now wants to know which פסוק teaches that exception.

keyTerms.meaning: Double payment that a thief must pay
From where are these things learned?

phrases.english: They have no double payment, and so on.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה: slaves, documents, land, and consecrated property.

phrases.english: From where are these matters learned?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין בָּהֶן תַּשְׁלוּמֵי כֶפֶל וְכוּ׳. מְנָהָנֵי מִילֵּי?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רבית discussion and opens a new section on the next clause of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source that עבדים, שטרות, קרקעות, and הקדש are excluded from תשלומי כפל.

steps.title: The verse of double payment: general, specific, general
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads the פסוק of כפל as a כלל ופרט וכלל: 'any matter of trespass' is a general term, 'ox, donkey, sheep, garment' are details, and 'any lost thing' is general again.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the Rabbis taught: 'For any matter of trespass' is a general statement. 'For an ox, for a donkey, for a sheep, for a garment' is a detail. 'For any lost thing about which one shall say' generalizes again.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer with a ברייתא that splits the פסוק of כפל into general, specific, and general parts. The conclusion drawn from this pattern comes right after this part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the Torah gives a general term, then specific examples, then a general term again, we include only things that are similar to the examples. The examples here are movable items with value of their own. That is how the ברייתא will exclude land, slaves, and documents.

keyTerms.meaning: A general statement in a פסוק
A specific detail or example in a פסוק
It went back and made a general statement again
A matter of wrongdoing or trespass

steps.confusionAlert: The derivation is not finished yet. So far the ברייתא has only labeled the three parts of the פסוק. What they teach comes in the next lines.

phrases.english: As the Rabbis taught:
'For any matter of trespass' is a general statement,

phrases.aramaic: ״עַל שׁוֹר עַל חֲמוֹר עַל שֶׂה עַל שַׂלְמָה״ – פְּרָט,
phrases.english: 'for an ox, for a donkey, for a sheep, for a garment' is a detail,
'for any lost thing about which one shall say,'
it went back and generalized.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתָנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״עַל כׇּל דְּבַר פֶּשַׁע״ – כְּלָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins to answer the question of Step 12 by bringing a ברייתא that reads the פסוק of כפל.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is the כלל ופרט וכלל in the פסוק of כפל. The conclusion of the derivation continues in the following text.

steps.title: The rule: only things like the examples in the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא applies the rule of כלל ופרט וכלל. כפל only applies to items like the listed details: things that can be moved and have value in themselves.
steps.simpleTranslation: General, detail, general: you only include things similar to the detail. The details are movable items that are themselves valuable, so the law covers every movable item that is itself valuable.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא from the last step now finishes its reasoning. It shows what the general-detail-general pattern teaches us.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 13 the ברייתא found a general-detail-general pattern in the פסוק. Here it uses the rule for that pattern: the law reaches beyond the listed details, but only to things that are similar to them. The shared features are two: the item can be moved, and the item itself is worth money.

keyTerms.meaning: Similar to the detail. Only things like the listed examples are included.
Movable property
The object itself is worth money, not just what it stands for

phrases.english: A general term, a detail, and a general term:

phrases.aramaic: אִי אַתָּה דָן אֶלָּא כְּעֵין הַפְּרָט;
